It follows from Proposition 3.20 that the center of the twisted Yangian $Z({\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm})$ is contained in the center of the shifted twisted Yangian $Z({\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm}(\sigma))$. In fact, for any $\sigma$ we have

(8.23)

$Z({\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm})=Z({\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm}(\sigma)).$

Let $\mathfrak{c}=\mathfrak{gl}_{N}[z]^{\theta}$ denote the twisted current algebra defined in §2.2, $\mathfrak{c}_{\sigma}=\mathfrak{gl}_{N}[z]^{\theta}(\sigma)$ denote its subalgebra defined in §8.1, and $\mathfrak{c}_{r}$ denote the subalgebra of $\mathfrak{c}$ spanned by elements $xz^{s}$ with $s>r$. To establish (8.23) one must check the inclusion $Z({\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm}(\sigma))\subseteq Z({\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm})$ and, for this, it suffices to show $S(\mathfrak{c}_{\sigma})^{\mathfrak{c}_{\sigma}}\subseteq S(\mathfrak{c})^{\mathfrak{c}}$. By a slight modification of the argument for [Mol07, Lem 2.8.1] one can prove that $S(\mathfrak{c})^{\mathfrak{c}}=S(\mathfrak{c})^{\mathfrak{c}_{r}}$ for any $r\geqslant 0$. Picking $r$ large enough so that $\mathfrak{c}_{r}\subseteq\mathfrak{c}_{\sigma}$, we have $S(\mathfrak{c}_{\sigma})^{\mathfrak{c}_{\sigma}}\subseteq S(\mathfrak{c})^{\mathfrak{c}_{\sigma}}\subseteq S(\mathfrak{c})^{\mathfrak{c}_{r}}=S(\mathfrak{c})^{\mathfrak{c}}$.

9. Baby comultiplication

In this section, we establish a baby comultiplication, which is an algebra homomorphism from ${\mathscr{Y}}_{\mu}^{\pm}(\sigma)$ to ${\mathscr{Y}}_{\mu}^{\pm}(\dot{\sigma})\otimes\mathrm{U}(\mathfrak{gl}_{t})$. This provides a powerful technical tool for studying both structure and representation theory (cf. [BK08]).

9.1. The formulation

Assume $\sigma\neq 0$ and suppose $\mu=(\mu_{1},\ldots,\mu_{n})$ is the minimal admissible shape of $\sigma$. Let ${\mathscr{Y}}_{\mu}^{\pm}(\sigma)$ be the shifted twisted Yangian associated to $\sigma$ and $\mu$, where we assume $\mu$ to be even for ${\mathscr{Y}}_{\mu}^{-}(\sigma)$. Define $\dot{\sigma}:=(\dot{\mathfrak{s}}_{i,j})_{1\leqslant i,j\leqslant N}$ according to the following rule

(9.1)

$\dot{\mathfrak{s}}_{i,j}:=\begin{cases}\mathfrak{s}_{i,j}-1,& if i\leqslant N-\mu_{n}

By definition, $\dot{\sigma}$ is a symmetric shift matrix and $\mu$ is admissible for $\dot{\sigma}$. Therefore the definition of ${\mathscr{Y}}_{\mu}^{\pm}(\dot{\sigma})$ makes sense. Due to Theorem 8.2 we have the embedding ${\mathscr{Y}}_{\mu}^{\pm}(\sigma)\hookrightarrow{\mathscr{Y}}_{\mu}^{\pm}(\dot{\sigma})$, sending $H_{a;i,j}^{(r)}\mapsto\dot{H}_{a;i,j}^{(r)}$ and $B_{a;f,g}^{(s)}\mapsto\dot{B}_{a;f,g}^{(s)}$. Here and after we use $\dot{H}_{a;i,j}^{(r)}$, $\dot{B}_{a;f,g}^{(s)}$ to denote elements in ${\mathscr{Y}}_{\mu}^{\pm}(\dot{\sigma})$ to avoid possible confusion.

paper.title: Shifted twisted Yangians and finite $W$-algebras of classical type
paper.abstract: We introduce parabolic presentations of twisted Yangians of types AI and AII, interpolating between the R-matrix presentation and the Drinfeld presentation. Then we formulate and provide parabolic presentations for the shifted twisted Yangians. We define quotient algebras known as truncated shifted twisted Yangians and equip them with baby comultiplications, generalizing the work of Brundan and Kleshchev. PBW bases for all (truncated) shifted twisted Yangians of type AI and AII are established along the way. Applying the theory of universal equivariant quantizations of conic symplectic singularities we show that the truncated twisted shifted Yangian is isomorphic to the finite $W$-algebra which quantizes a suitable Slodowy slice. This provides a presentation of the finite $W$-algebra associated with every even nilpotent element in type {\sf B} and {\sf C}, as well as every nilpotent element with two Jordan blocks in type {\sf D}. Finally we make a conjecture which would supply presentations in the remaining even cases in type {\sf D}.
